literal: Naturally, strangers are not one's own people, when one's own possessing heart is not friendly.
translation: It is only natural that strangers do not act as our friends, when our very own heart does not stand by us.
modern: நம்முடைய சொந்த நெஞ்சமே நமக்குத் துணையாக இல்லாதபோது, அயலார் நமக்கு உறவினராக இல்லாமல் இருப்பது இயல்பானதே.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the behavior of her own heart, which constantly sides with her lover instead of supporting her. She reasons that when one's own heart (neñcam) does not act as a loyal friend (tamar al vaḻi), it is completely natural (tañcam) that strangers (ētilār) do not show any friendliness (tamar allar) either. The word 'tañcam' is used here in the sense of 'easy' or 'no wonder', emphasizing that internal betrayal makes external indifference entirely expected. This poignant observation highlights the deep internal conflict of a lover whose mind refuses to cooperate with her resolve.
